newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says it takes no position on Brcko.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says it takes no position on Brcko.

text.p: The State Department said on Wednesday it had taken no position on the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko, which is the subject of international arbitration.

U.S. officials did not deny that an internal paper on the subject existed but they said they understood it reported the views of others or contained options and did not reflect the U.S. view on the sensitive issue of control over Brcko.

Earlier, diplomats in Sarajevo said U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum had proposed in a policy statement that the arbitration panel award the strategic town to the Bosnian Serbs, who seized the area four years ago.
Such a move would almost certainly provoke an angry response from Bosnia's U.S.-backed Moslem-Croat federation.

But State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said: "There is no U.S. proposal for a Brcko solution. There's no paper by John Kornblum ... no paper by any other senior department official advocating a particular position before the arbitral tribunal."
Davies added: "The question of Brcko arbitration is a matter for the arbitral tribunal."

The U.S.-brokered Dayton peace agreement of 1995, which ended Bosnia's war between Serbs, Moslems and Croats, failed to resolve the future status of Brcko and called for arbitration. The Rome-based panel, chaired by American lawyer Roberts Owen, must deliver a decision by Feb. 15.
A senior U.S. official conceded that a U.S. internal document was in circulation.

"From what I understand it may be some kind of a discussion paper that reports on the state of play, reports on the views of others, and perhaps contains options," said the official, who spoke on condition he was not identified.
"There's no U.S. view of the Brcko matter contained in this paper."

The narrow Brcko land corridor, which links Serb territory to the west and east, is considered vulnerable to attack. Military analysts say if NATO peace enforcement troops leave as scheduled in mid-1998 war could easily erupt there, barring a prior settlement.
Federation leaders in Sarajevo say Brcko should be placed in the federation because Moslems and Croats formed a majority of the population before the 1992-95 war.
